title: Selection
description: What dialback_ledger.select_number(case) returns, and what ledger.number_selections stores: the number a case will call, up to two alternates, or no_provable_number, plus every candidate the rule looked at and why it was or wasn't eligible. Owner: Inesh. The core reads number_selection_id, rule_version, contact_point_id, reason and source_types (spec 0002, D11). Rules: phone numbers only, in E.164; never a bank account number (ADR-8); numbers are integers; a selection reads only rows recorded before the cutoff and stores a hash of them, so it can be replayed.

number_selection_id.description: The ledger.number_selections row this document is stored in.

rule_version.description: The selection rule that ran, e.g. ledger-select-v1. The stub reports ledger-stub-v0.

requested_cutoff.description: The cutoff the core passed (the change's detection time).

cutoff.description: The cutoff the rule used: the earliest of the request's arrival, the first message from a lookalike domain and the change appearing in Ramp, never later than requested_cutoff. Our own receive times only, never a printed date or an email's Date: header.

outcome.description: picked: call contact_point_id. no_provable_number: no call; the case goes to needs_review (R7).

contact_point_id.description: The chosen ledger.contact_points row. Present only when outcome is picked.

e164.description: The chosen number. Present only when outcome is picked.

source_types.description: The independent source types behind the chosen number (copied into number_resolved).

alternates.description: Eligible runners-up in rank order, used only if the chosen number is dead. Present only when outcome is picked.

reason.description: Why no number was picked, for a person. Required when outcome is no_provable_number.

candidates.description: Every phone number the rule considered for this vendor, eligible or not, in rank order (eligible first).

inputs_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical (RFC 8785) list of ledger rows the rule read, so the selection can be replayed and checked.

SourceType.description: How a value reached us, from custody metadata, never from a model (ADR-13). All email counts as one source type. The old vendor master's number on file is never a source type; see Candidate.on_file.

Role.description: The line's role as the labeler read it.

Reason.description: Why a candidate isn't eligible. first_seen_in_change_context: R2. too_few_source_types: fewer than rule_settings.min_source_types before the cutoff. younger_than_minimum_age: first seen less than rule_settings.min_age_days before the cutoff. near_miss_of_older_number: one digit off, or two swapped digits away from, an older vendor number, and not an established sibling line. hidden_text_only: seen only in text a person couldn't see (white, tiny or off-page). not_vendor_party: labeled as the customer's or a bank's number. fax_line: labeled as a fax.

first_seen_at.description: Our receive time of the earliest observation before the cutoff.

source_types.description: Independent source types seen before the cutoff.

on_file.description: The old vendor master lists this number. Shown, never counted.

observation_count.description: Observations before the cutoff that this candidate rests on.

near_miss_of.description: The older contact point this number is a near miss of, when reasons has near_miss_of_older_number.

rank.description: 1 is the pick. Present only on eligible candidates.

RuleSettings.description: The settings the rule ran with; the ablations vary these.

min_source_types.description: Independent source types needed before the cutoff (v1: 2).

min_age_days.description: Days the number must have been seen before the cutoff (v1: 90).

near_miss_distance.description: Edit distance, in digits, that counts as a near miss (v1: 1, plus one swap of adjacent digits).

same_subject_window_days.description: A message with the request's subject line within this many days counts as change context (v1: 30).
